A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across the revisions.

before.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix G report original MCMC simulations, MountainCar linearity experiments, and synthetic Markov-chain stopping-time comparisons.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional false-alarm estimation and stopping-time/runtime experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, its statistic and stopping boundary, and the two-sided construction are unchanged. The surrogate retains its optimization objective and weighted-median solution; revisions concern the optimizer's statement and derivation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MCMC misspecification, discretized MountainCar linearity, and the same synthetic exponential-family testing problem. The added state-size sweeps vary configurations within that synthetic family.

E2.justification: Appendix G.4 and Figures 6–7 retain the same Fields et al. comparisons, including the Modified Jeffreys variant. Newly cited UCB, KL-UCB, and IMED methods are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix G.3 adds runtime-per-step evaluations for m = 32, 64, 128 at alpha = 0.05 and for alpha = 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 at m = 64. Appendix G.1 adds importance sampling from Qbad, with likelihood-ratio weighting, to estimate rejection under Qgood. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses investigate rare false alarms despite observing no direct null rejections, and sensitivity of stopping time and computation to state count and error level. These supplement the retained feature-dimension and stopping-time analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a 1,000-run importance-sampling estimate with a reported 95% confidence interval. Its stated MCMC run counts change from 50 to 100, matching figures already labeled 100 runs in v1; this does not establish that additional runs occurred. Existing three-standard-deviation bands remain.

E6.justification: New results include a false-alarm estimate reported as (1.21 ± 2.12) × 10^-30 and Tables 2–3 of stopping times and runtimes. At alpha = 0.05, Table 2 reports mean stopping times 665.65, 2516.84, and 9700.55 for m = 32, 64, and 128. The original comparison curves are retained; these additions do not demonstrate improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Proposition D.1 replaces v1's asserted strict duality gap and constrained min-max argument with a KKT derivation and explicit threshold-feasibility analysis. This revises supporting mathematical reasoning for the existing surrogate optimizer; the main lower-bound and optimality theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim non-asymptotic instance-dependent lower bounds, asymptotically optimal composite testing, and the same applications. The revised abstract explicitly says finite-state and asymptotically tight, making qualifications already present in v1's setup and guarantees clearer.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an analogy suggesting Pinsker-based surrogates might retain order optimality with worse constants, while explicitly leaving this unproved for Markovian data. Section 6 additionally identifies direct use of the mixture martingale as an open computational-statistical question.

D1.justification: The new timing experiments disclose Google Colab and an Intel Xeon 2.20 GHz CPU with one core and two logical CPUs. Appendix G.1 also documents the likelihood-ratio estimator. Existing MountainCar hyperparameters and CVXPY information are retained.

R1.justification: New references support the UCB/KL-UCB/IMED analogy and KKT argument, including Auer, Cappé, Honda–Takemura, Agrawal et al. (2021b), and Vishnoi. The Bertsekas book is replaced by a different work. Positioning relative to Fields et al. remains unchanged; the Russo citation receives a publication update.

P1.justification: Localized edits refine the abstract and computational discussion, rewrite part of Appendix D, and expand acknowledgements. Theorem 4.1's main-text proof sketch is removed, with its full Appendix B proof retained. The overall section and appendix structure remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2–3, enlarges Figure 1, and removes Figure 4's empty stopping-time panel while updating its caption. Algorithm 1 and several displays shift position through reflow; the other plots retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 removes the erroneous duality-gap assertion, supplies a more explicit optimizer derivation, reconciles MCMC run reporting, and adds evidence about false alarms and computational scaling. These improve exposition and empirical support. The gains are limited by a sign typo in the new KKT analysis and incomplete specification of the larger-state experiments.
